evidence.claim: Passport holders of countries with visa-exemption arrangements (incl. the US, per corroborating sources) may enter Japan visa-free for tourism, stays of 90 days or less
Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (mofa.go.jp) states 90-day visa exemption for reciprocal-arrangement countries incl. the US
Visit Japan Web is the official digital pre-registration system for immigration/customs; not mandatory, paper cards still accepted
Seven Bank ATMs (28,000+ at 7-Eleven stores nationwide) accept foreign-issued Visa/Plus/Mastercard/Maestro/Cirrus/UnionPay/Amex/JCB/Discover/Diners cards, 24/7, English-language screen

Japan's instant point-of-sale tax exemption for tourists remains in effect through Oct 31, 2026; a refund-at-departure system replaces it Nov 1, 2026 — this trip (Oct 19–23) falls entirely under the current instant-exemption system
Fukuoka Airport's International Terminal (1F, landside) hosts a Sakura Mobile SIM/pocket-wifi counter (7:00–21:00) and a separate Global WiFi/Ninja WiFi counter

Japan's emergency numbers are 110 (police) and 119 (ambulance/fire), free 24/7 from any phone; JNTO runs a 24/7 multilingual visitor hotline at 050-3816-2787; #7119 triages non-urgent medical questions
Matsumoto Kiyoshi drugstore operates a branch inside Fukuoka Airport's International Terminal (3F), hours 7:30–18:00
US State Department travel advisory level for Japan could not be confirmed — travel.state.gov blocks automated access
JMA 1991–2020 climate normals for Fukuoka in October: average temp 19.6°C, average max 23.7°C, average min 16.0°C, average precipitation 94.5mm for the month
No Japanese national public holiday falls between Oct 19–23, 2026 — nearest holidays are Sports Day (Oct 12) and Culture Day (Nov 3)
Hakata Okunchi runs on fixed annual dates, Oct 23–24, at Kushida Shrine — harvest market and free amazake 10:00–16:00 on Oct 23, ox-cart mikoshi procession Oct 24; free admission
Dazaifu Tenmangu's major annual festival, Jinkosai, is confirmed for Sept 21–25, 2026 — a month before this trip's Oct 19–23 window
Over 100 yatai stalls operate around Fukuoka City, concentrated in Nagahama and Tenjin (Nakasu commonly cited as a third cluster in secondary sources)
Most yatai open ≈18:00–19:00 (a few as early as 18:00), closing around midnight; stalls may not open in stormy weather or if the owner is unwell
Fukuoka City's official yatai guide recommends groups of 2–3; large groups may not be able to enter due to limited seating
A typical yatai stall has roughly 8–10 total seats, including all other customers present
A typical yatai stall has roughly 6–10 total seats — consistent with the 8–10 figure from an independent source
Most yatai only accept cash — only about 10% of stalls accept credit cards
Tell the owner your headcount before sitting; wait for the whole group to arrive before joining the queue; order roughly one drink and one dish per person; pay by asking for the bill at the end
If a seat is held for a long time without much ordering when the stall is busy, someone else may lose their chance — turnover is a real etiquette expectation, don't linger once finished
Turnover pressure at a busy yatai is real — don't stay too long, and free your seat promptly once you're finished eating
Ichiran's Nakasu Souhonten (head shop/office) is at 5-3-2 Nakasu, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka; open 24 hours, subject to change without notice
Ichiran's tonkotsu recipe dates to 1960, per the chain's own "Since 1960" tagline and company history page
Ichiran began in Nakasu in 1960 as a ramen stall named "Futaba Ramen," renamed Ichiran in 1966 — corroborating that the Nakasu Souhonten sits at the brand's founding location
Ippudo Daimyo Main Store is at 1-13-14 Daimyo, Chuo-ku, Fukuoka-shi

Ippudo Daimyo Honten hours (Mon–Thu 11:00–23:00, Fri/holidays 11:00–24:00, Sat 10:30–24:00, Sun 10:30–23:00) surfaced via search synthesis referencing stores.ippudo.com, but a direct fetch of that same URL only rendered a last-orders note, not the full table — treated as unconfirmed
Motsunabe (offal hot pot) is a hallmark Fukuoka-Hakata dish; a common local custom finishes the meal by adding champon noodles to the leftover broth ("shime")
Motsunabe Rakutenchi (2-5-23 Hakata Ekimae, Hakata-ku) has run 44 years, hours 17:00–24:00 (last order 23:30), with counter seating plus a tatami area
Fukuya, founded by Toshio Kawahara, first sold karashi mentaiko in 1949 from a small Nakasu, Hakata grocery store — credited as the originator of modern mentaiko; the recipe was never patented
Fukuya's Nakasu main store is at 2-6-10 Nakasu, Hakata-ku; hours weekdays 9:00–22:00, Sundays/holidays 9:30–18:00
Daichan (Gion Daichan), a yatai specializing in udon, is listed at 1-8 Nakasu, Hakata-ku, ≈10-min walk from Nakasu-Kawabata Station Exit 1; cards not accepted

Hakata is traditionally credited as the birthplace of udon (and soba) in Japan — a stone monument at Jotenji Temple marks the claim, attributed to 13th-century Zen monk Shoichi Kokushi (Enni Ben'en), who brought milling techniques back from Song-dynasty China in 1241
Jotenji Temple's founding (completed 1242) and Enni's role bringing back flour-milling technique are corroborated independently
Itoshima's oyster huts (kaki-goya) serve fresh grilled oysters roughly October through April
Shiki no Chaya, an on-site restaurant at Shiraito Falls, serves yamame (mountain trout) set meals and hand-pulled soba; seasonal nagashi somen from early summer through autumn

Canal City Hakata shop/restaurant hours and its fountain show schedule could only be sourced via search snippets — canalcity.co.jp returned HTTP 403 on 3 direct fetch attempts (root EN page, fountain-show page, events page)
Dazaifu Tenmangu shrine grounds are free to enter; opens ≈6:30 AM in autumn (spring-equinox-to-autumn-equinox window opens 6:00 AM), closes ≈19:00 in autumn depending on exact seasonal cutover

Dazaifu Tenmangu's Treasure Hall admission: adults ¥500, university/HS ¥200, JHS/elementary ¥100. Kanko Rekishikan museum: adults ¥200, university/HS ¥150, JHS/elementary ¥100. Both open 9:00–16:30, last entry 16:00
The shrine's own site recommends dawn (near opening) or dusk for a quieter visit, ahead of tour-bus traffic
Dazaifu Tenmangu's Omotesando approach street is lined with shops selling umegae mochi, the local grilled-mochi specialty, alongside cafes and souvenir stores

Kyushu National Museum: 9:30–17:00 (last entry 16:30), extended Saturdays during special exhibitions; closed Mondays (or the following day if Monday is a holiday); regular collection admission ¥700, free under-18 and 70+
No special exhibition runs during Oct 19–23, 2026 — the prior special exhibit closed Oct 4, 2026, and the next opens Oct 31, 2026; only the ¥700 regular collection is viewable during the trip
Maizuru Park (Fukuoka Castle Ruins) hours: Apr–Sep 9:00–19:00, Oct–Mar 9:00–18:00, closed Dec 29–Jan 3; free access to grounds/ruins
Ohori Park: ~398,000 sqm with a 226,000 sqm pond, opened 1927, a ~2km path circles the pond; free, always accessible

Kushida Shrine main hall accessible 4:00–22:00, free admission; a ≈13m ornamental Hakata Gion Yamakasa float is on free, year-round display except during June; founded 757 CE, with a 1,000+ year old ginkgo tree
Sakurai Futamigaura (the ocean torii/"husband and wife rocks") is free public beach/shrine access; the sacred rocks sit ≈150m offshore, part of Sakurai Shrine; paid parking ≈¥300/hour, ≈47 spaces
Shiraito Falls is free, a 24m drop at 530m elevation on Mt. Hagane; the adjacent Fureai no Sato facility runs 9:00–17:00 (extended to 18:00 Jul–Aug)
Nokonoshima Island Park hours: weekdays 9:00–17:30, Sundays/holidays 9:00–18:30; open year-round with no closed days

Nokonoshima Island Park admission (≈¥1,500 adult, per one aggregator) could not be confirmed against an official source — nokonoshima.com returned only page titles with no body content on 4 fetch attempts, and gofukuoka.jp's listing doesn't state a price
The Fukuoka City Subway Airport (Kuko) Line connects directly to Fukuoka Airport's Domestic Terminal via escalator; the International Terminal requires the free shuttle bus first

The free shuttle bus between Fukuoka Airport's International and Domestic Terminals runs every 5–6 min at peak (7:00–18:00), 6–15 min off-peak; the North Bus Stop at the Domestic Terminal is discontinued since Dec 3, 2024 (South Bus Stop only, construction-related)
Fukuoka City Subway fare from the Airport to both Hakata and Tenjin is ¥260 (adult); Airport→Hakata ≈5 min, Airport→Tenjin ≈11 min

Nimoca IC card costs ¥2,000 total (¥500 deposit + ¥1,500 credit), top-up to ¥20,000; refund fee ¥220, not available at the Airport's International Terminal; nationwide cards (Suica, Pasmo, Icoca, Sugoca) work interchangeably on Fukuoka transit
IC card boarding is per-person, not group-batched — each rider taps in/out individually at the gate; no group-gate mechanism exists
Reaching Dazaifu by train from Nishitetsu Fukuoka (Tenjin) requires the Tenjin-Omuta Line to Nishitetsu-Futsukaichi, then a transfer to the Dazaifu Line — no through train exists

The Nishitetsu Dazaifu Liner "Tabito" runs direct, no-transfer, from Hakata Bus Terminal (¥800, ≈40 min) and Fukuoka Airport's International Terminal (¥700, ≈25 min); ¥20 IC/card discount; no reservation; 28 trips/day weekdays, 36–37 weekends; can deny boarding once full

Nishitetsu raised fares system-wide effective Apr 1, 2026 (base fare ¥170→¥180, ¥60 fare bands) on the Tenjin-Omuta and Dazaifu lines — the pre-revision Tenjin-Dazaifu figure (¥400) is now stale; a post-revision figure of ≈¥480 appears only in an aggregator projection, not independently confirmed against Nishitetsu's own dynamic fare-search tool

The JR Chikuhi Line runs from Meinohama through Itoshima (Chikuzen-Maebaru, Chikuzen-Fukae) toward Karatsu; train stations do not reach the coastal sights (Sakurai Futamigaura, Shiraito Falls) directly

Showa Bus's Itoshima Sunset Line and Nishinoura Line connect Nishinoura/Chikuzen-Maebaru to Keya, serving Futamigaura and Nogita; a separate Keya Line runs Maebaru Station North Exit → Keya (≈26 min) — exact frequency and fares couldn't be extracted (PDF/binary, unparseable)
The "Futamigaura Meoto-iwa-mae" Showa Bus stop is discontinued and replaced by "Okuguchi Sakurai Shrine West Entrance" on multiple coastal routes, effective Apr 4, 2026 — in effect for this trip

Fukuoka City Municipal Ferry, Meinohama→Nokonoshima: adult one-way ¥230, 10 min, ≈23 daily departures (21 Sundays/holidays), roughly hourly, first ≈5:00, last ≈23:00; a connecting Nishitetsu bus (≈10 min) reaches the park itself

JR Chikuhi Line's own timetable subdomain returned a Saturday schedule (last observed departure from Chikuzen-Maebaru toward Fukuoka Airport/Meinohama/Hakata: 23:10) despite requesting a weekday view twice — weekday last-train time for Oct 19–23, 2026 (all weekdays) is unconfirmed

Nishitetsu's own printable per-station timetable (updated for the Mar 14, 2026 schedule revision) exists at a known official URL but is image/vector-encoded and could not be parsed for the exact last-train time from Dazaifu

transport.route: Chikuzen-Maebaru Station ↔ Sakurai Futamigaura / Shiraito Falls (Showa Bus + taxi)
transport.doorToDoor: From central Fukuoka: JR Chikuhi Line to Chikuzen-Maebaru (≈40–50 min), then a sparse Showa Bus connection or a taxi for the final leg to each coastal sight — no single transit leg covers the whole route.
transport.transferReality: Bus frequency on the coastal routes (Nishinoura Line, Itoshima Sunset Line) is low, and exact daily frequency couldn't be confirmed this pass — the fare/schedule PDFs were unparseable. The Sakurai Futamigaura stop itself is being renamed from 'Futamigaura Meoto-iwa-mae' to 'Okuguchi Sakurai Shrine West Entrance' effective Apr 4, 2026, already in effect for this trip.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: A party of 8 relying on a single sparse bus is itself a capacity risk on top of the frequency problem — two taxis or a rental van is the more reliable way to move the whole group between sights in one day, which is why the guide recommends that directly.
transport.buffer: Plan to leave the coast by early evening rather than targeting a specific last bus or train precisely.
transport.missedConnection: A missed bus connection back to Chikuzen-Maebaru likely means a long wait for the next one, or calling a taxi from a rural stop — inconvenient, not stranding, but a real risk given the sparse service this pass couldn't fully quantify.
transport.nextService: ⚠ Not confirmed this pass — Showa Bus's fare/frequency documents were PDF/binary and unreadable by the fetch tool used.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: ⚠ Not confirmed this pass for the specific weekday — plan to be back at Chikuzen-Maebaru well before dark rather than relying on an unverified last-service time.
transport.fallback: Taxi is the practical fallback for the whole day, not just emergencies — reflected directly in the guide's own recommendation to use a taxi or rental car rather than public transit for this leg.

reservations.notApplicableReason: No shipped or detour candidate this pass is a scarce-release booking — every shipped food pick is walk-in (yatai take no reservations by design), Dazaifu Tenmangu and the sights are free/no-ticket, and Kyushu National Museum and Nokonoshima sell same-day. Nothing clears the reservation-depth bar.

saturation.note: Across four parallel research batches (logistics/entry/money/health, transit, Dazaifu/Itoshima sights, Fukuoka food/yatai), later searches within each topic converged on the same core set of official sources and named venues rather than surfacing new serious contenders — e.g. Nakasu kept resurfacing as the shared hub for Ichiran, Fukuya and yatai across three independent search threads, and Itoshima's coastal-sight list (Sakurai Futamigaura, Shiraito Falls) was stable across both the sights-focused and transit-focused batches. Remaining gaps (exact post-revision Nishitetsu fare, Showa Bus frequencies, exact last-train times, the US State Dept advisory level, Nokonoshima's admission price) are all read-only precision gaps on facts already directionally established — none of them would change which venues, routes, or days are recommended, only refine a number or a flag. The one genuinely unresolved item with a small chance of mattering — Hakata Okunchi's exact 2026 program, inferred from a consistent multi-year date pattern rather than a 2026-dated announcement — is already treated as optional, flight-time-dependent color on the departure day rather than a fixed commitment, so an eventual correction wouldn't restructure the itinerary.
